item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
488
ABPZ20 KNHC 071712
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Sep 7 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located a few hundred miles southwest of Lihue, Hawaii, and
on Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Punta Eugenia, Mexico.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms associated with a
trough of low pressure is located several hundred miles
south-southwest of southwestern Mexico. Gradual development of this
system is possible, and a tropical depression could form later this
week while the system moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Public Advisory Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 072032
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Marie Advisory Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 PM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026
 
...DANGEROUS BEACH CONDITIONS EXPECTED ALONG THE COAST OF BAJA
CALIFORNIA AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA FOR THE NEXT COUPLE OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...24.8N 125.3W
ABOUT 665 MI...1070 KM WSW OF PUNTA EUGENIA MEXICO
ABOUT 735 MI...1185 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was
located near latitude 24.8 North, longitude 125.3 West. Marie is
moving toward the west-northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A turn to the
northwest is forecast to occur over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Steady weakening is expected for the next couple of days, and Marie
is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low on Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of the Baja California Peninsula and southern California
for the next couple of days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 072033
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 PM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026
 
Visible satellite imagery depicts Marie as a sheared system with a
low-level center that has recently become exposed to the northwest
of the convective area. The latest subjective Dvorak intensity
estimate from TAFB was 45 kt, while objective estimates from CIMSS
range from 38-52 kt. A recent ASCAT pass from METOP-B revealed max
winds near Marie's center at around 45 kt. Given the typical low
bias in ASCAT due to its resolution, the initial intensity was set
at 50 kt.
 
Marie's initial motion estimate was 285/7 kt. The storm has moved
more westward since the last advisory, but is still forecast to turn
to the northwest as a cutoff low from the northeast Pacific dives
down and interacts with Marie. The official NHC track forecast
shifted slightly leftward due to the more westward initial motion,
and is reflected mostly by a blend of the previous official forecast
and HCCA.
 
The timing of Marie transitioning into a post-tropical storm was
moved up to 36 h as the cyclone moves into an increasingly hostile
environment, and IR satellite imagery continues to depict degrading
convection. The latest NHC intensity forecast continues to hasten
Marie's weakening within the first 24 h, before weakening becomes
more gradual upon the storm's post-tropical transition. This
forecast generally falls in line with the model consensus.
